name: precond_pre_slot0
label: mech:precond
rationale: Highest-value arm: all three agents ranked it first, it is zero-build and structurally zero-throughput, and it is LR-neutral because the control's final_scale is norm-preserving so both arms deliver an update of Frobenius norm ~sqrt(min(m,n)). Mechanism is MuonEq-R with a beta2=0.95 EMA (critic's taxonomy, NOT Muon2), and it is TWO aligned factors: removes output-side NorMuon adaptivity and adds input-side equilibration. name: wd040_slot0
label: knob:wd_const
rationale: Zero build, zero throughput. The critic's magnitude over the pragmatist's bracket because only one arm fits in 12 runs and +0.3 above the baseline's integrated mean of 0.1 is 3x the leverage of the 0.0 arm. Mechanistically live: 1/(2*eta*lambda)=62 steps at eta=0.04 lambda=0.2 against ~1015 steps, so equilibrium is reached. Cautious decay of 2D params makes this D-Muon-like, which is the regime where b2_large_weight_decay_wins_at_short_training_horizons (4/4) applies rather than b2_muon_2d_params_break_the_large_weight_decay_rule. falsifier: No weight-norm observable exists, so a NULL here cannot be separated from 'decay applied, weights never moved' and must NOT be recorded as a closed axis until muon_weight_rms is built. A non-null IS interpretable because engagement is guaranteed by construction, unlike clip. Void the pair if treatment and control land on different final_epoch: L005 bites hardest on a regularizer at the 2-epoch boundary.
expected: SIGN GENUINELY UNKNOWN and left open by this council: undertraining at ~4 TPP points to Moonlight's no-WD-converges-faster, repeated tokens at final_epoch 2.0 point to regularization helping. Magnitude |0.0005| to |0.002| after dilution to the 25M Muon-governed parameters. wd_const=0.0 runs next round regardless of the outcome.

label: mech:zloss
rationale: z-loss at lambda=0.1. A registered claim reports lambda=1e-4 is an exact null while lambda=1e-1 moves optimal loss ~0.02 nats at 57M-221M, and the generator already has a zloss branch that has never been run. name: R2V_A_s0_treat
label: knob:ve
rationale: Value embedding on EVERY layer instead of every other (ve stride 2 -> 1), doubling tables 4->8 and adding ~16.8M parameters. ve is a STRIDE, not a count: ve=1 is the DENSER setting. Restored to QUAD waves the moment gpu4-7 freed together -- the treatment then occupies every device within a single wave, so the 0.00049 device offset cancels WITHIN the wave rather than across waves, and host drift between waves cannot load onto the effect. Registered literature leans negative here.
falsifier: The four same-GPU deltas disagree in sign, or the counterbalanced mean lands inside the 0.000271 resolution. Registered claims oppose: all-layers injection has been measured worse than single-layer, and dense per-layer expansion saturates at 0.006 loss for +32% FLOPs.
expected: val_bpb changes by more than 0.000271 as a GPU-counterbalanced mean; the sign says whether the second table pair earns its parameters and its memory traffic.

name: R2S_A_s0_treat
label: knob:swdiv
rationale: Halve the SSSL short-attention span (swdiv 2 -> 4). Recomputed from baseline/train.py estimate_flops over the real window list at sequence_len 2048, this removes 18.87M of 239.08 MFLOP/token -- 7.9% of the total, NOT the 26% attention represents as a whole (L033); the two long-window layers holding 40% of the attention term are untouched. An independent harness using the identical S/L abstraction defines its short window as T/4 and reports val_bpb 0.895 for it against 0.895 for full attention. Quad waves restored now that gpu4-7 are free together.
falsifier: num_steps does not rise above the yoked control -- the FLOP removal bought nothing and the arm is INCONCLUSIVE, exactly as ns=3 was. Or val_bpb rises by more than the step gain is worth under the control-only step law of -0.05974 per e-fold.
expected: val_bpb lower by at least 0.0006 as a GPU-counterbalanced mean, carried by a step-count gain; under the corrected 7.9% arithmetic that needs nearly the whole step gain to survive.

name: R3U_A_s0_treat
label: mech:unet
rationale: First test in signal_path, a family with zero runs. Zero-initialised U-net skips from the lower half of the stack to the upper half: the variant starts numerically identical to the control and adds one elementwise add per lower-half layer, no matmul. name: R2S2_A_s0_treat
label: knob:swdiv
rationale: REPAIR of the swdiv counterbalancing broken by a device-set shift (L036). R2S_B launched on gpu1/4/5/6 instead of gpu4-7 because gpu7 had not released, putting the treatment on gpu4 twice and never on gpu7 in the swap; gpu1 then took a foreign tenant and died rc=1. verdict.py correctly refuses a verdict from that. This pair re-runs both layouts so the treatment occupies every device once. Confirm from each result's gpu field that the waves actually landed on the same four devices before reading any mean -- do not assume they did, which is the whole content of L036.
falsifier: flops_per_token_M is not below 230 (the edit did not apply; control computes 239.078, swdiv=4 computes 220.204). Or num_steps fails to rise above the yoked control, making the arm INCONCLUSIVE about the trade as ns=3 was. Or val_bpb rises by more than the step gain is worth under the control-only step law of -0.05974 per e-fold. Or arms finish at different final_epoch (L005).
expected: val_bpb lower by at least 0.0006 as a GPU-counterbalanced mean. Uncounterbalanced evidence so far has all four treatments beating their own device's control mean by -0.0017 to -0.0023 with step gains of +2.9% to +3.8%, so the repair should confirm rather than overturn -- but the offset it removes is the same size as the effects this campaign chases.

name: R5T18_A_s0_treat

expected: val_bpb lower by at least 0.002, about 7x resolution, with roughly doubled num_steps.

name: R5MC_A_s0_treat
label: knob:mu_ceil+tbs

Our tbs=18 arm inherited the baseline 0.95, so by that rule it has been running a momentum coefficient too small for its batch. Distinct from R5MU, which holds the ramp FRACTION fixed; this moves the CEILING.

expected: A further 0.00028 or more beyond tbs=18 alone. The prior is deliberately modest: the rule is a bound-proxy asymptotic with no language-model verification, transfer scored 2.

expected: val_bpb moves by more than 0.00028 in either direction; sign is the finding.

name: R5T17_A_s0_treat
label: knob:dbs+tbs
rationale: Rung 2 of the downward tbs sweep, REBUILT with dbs=64. The first version specified dbs=128, which violates the assert at baseline/train.py:503 -- TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE must divide DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*MAX_SEQ_LEN, and 131072/(128*2048)=0.5. All 8 runs would have crashed; an independent audit caught it before any GPU time was spent. Note dbs=64 is a second changed factor, but it holds grad_accum at 1 -- the same value tbs=18 already runs at -- so the accumulation depth is constant across rungs 1 and 2 and only tokens_per_step moves.
falsifier: Marginal over tbs=18 inside +/-0.000280 -> SATURATED, close the sweep. Or val_bpb RISES above tbs=18, meaning we have passed the critical batch size and 262144 was the floor. Or different final_epoch (L005), the live hazard since tbs=18 already sits at 508.0M against a ~510M boundary. Or the dbs=64 change carries its own effect, which a later dbs-only arm at fixed tbs would have to separate.
expected: A further 0.000280 or more beyond tbs=18, step count roughly doubling again to ~4000.
